text:
maria: Hey team — quick sync. Onboarding for the llama-compat weights landed: gs://redwood-models/onboard/llama-compat/v1/weights.tar.gz. Can we validate tokenizer + prompt-template behavior before we flip serving?

deepak: Thanks. Quick repro I hit locally — leading newline gets an extra token: tokenize('\nHello') -> [<bos>, <nl>, 'Hello'] vs expected [<bos>, 'Hello']. Wondering if our tokenizer loader is preserving leading whitespace.

ryan: I'll run a local pass on the tokenizer. Maria, does the weights bundle include the tokenizer vocab/tokenizer.json or is it referenced in the manifest?

maria: It includes tokenizer.json at the root: gs://redwood-models/onboard/llama-compat/v1/tokenizer.json and model-config.yaml. Note the model-config has a chat_template like: '<<SYS>>{system}\\n{user}' — please validate sentinel mappings with that.

sasha: FYI our chat-format layer strips leading whitespace by default (we normalize messages). That explains the newline discrepancy — if we want exact preservation we should opt-in with a config flag `preserve_leading_newlines: true`.

deepak: I'll add a unit test in tokenizers/tests/test_onboard_tokenizer.py. Minimal snippet: ```
# repro
assert tokenize('\nHello') == [BOS, NL, 'Hello']
```
Also noticed eos id mismatch: model checkpoint reports eos_id=2 but some toolchains expect 1. Need canonical special token mapping in the model-config.

ryan: Opening a tiny PR to add tests and config changes. Also CI reported a lint failure: deploy-bot says `serve: config validation failed: unknown key 'sentinel_mode'` — looks like model-config.yaml contains a field not in runtime schema.

deploy-bot: config-lint: errors=1, warnings=0 — unknown field 'sentinel_mode' at model-config.yaml:line 12

maria: We used `sentinel_mode` during an experiment. I'll remove it and convert to a supported field. For rollout plan: can we do a canary that sets `token_transform: preserve_newline` and fallback to default? I'll add env var `REDWOOD_ONBOARD_PRESERVE_NEWLINE=true` to the canary.

sasha: Also recommend adding explicit `special_tokens` mapping in model-config to avoid id/name mismatches. Example: `{"bos": "<s>", "eos": "</s>", "pad": "<pad>"}` — our loader currently maps empty string '' -> '' and that sometimes creates duplicate BOS insertions.

deepak: Ran tests locally: with `preserve_leading_newlines=true` and explicit special token mapping the tokenizer output matches expected across our chat templates. I'll push test outputs to the PR.

ryan: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/482 — added tests, removed sentinel_mode, added special_tokens mapping, and bumped weights path to gs://redwood-models/onboard/llama-compat/v1/weights_v2.tar.gz (we applied a quick quant step). Ping @maria for review.

maria: LGTM. Scheduling canary tomorrow 09:00 PST. Quick checklist before canary: validate config-lint clean, confirm token ids match runtime mapping, run 1k sample prompt set through canary and check log for unexpected <bos>/<eos> placement. Thanks all :tada:

ryan: I'll run the 1k sample sweep and provide a small report in the PR as a comment.

sasha: One more note — when you run the sweep, include messages that start with emojis and markdown (e.g., `:wave:` and `*bold*`) — some tokenizers treat emoji as leading tokens and that changes alignment for prompt truncation.

maria: Good call. Adding that to canary checklist. If anything blocks, we pause and revert to hosted-v1.

deepak: PR updated with test artifacts. If folks are happy I'll merge after Maria's LGTM.

maria: Final LGTM given the test coverage and config fixes. Merging after CI passes. Will monitor canary metrics (latency, token mismatch rate) during rollout. Thanks team! :white_check_mark:
